content: Lansoprazole has the potential to interact with other medications and supplements. Before starting lansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are currently using. For more detailed information, refer to the Interactions section. It is not known whether lansoprazole can affect pregnancy or harm an unborn baby. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. They will determine whether you should take lansoprazole during pregnancy or while trying to conceive. Do not take lansoprazole while breastfeeding, as it can pass into breast milk. Lansoprazole should be taken before meals. It is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects lansoprazole. Always inform your healthcare provider about any prescription or OTC medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using. Certain medications, such as methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, theophylline, clarithromycin, tacrolimus, antiretroviral drugs (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin, may interact with lansoprazole. These interactions can alter the blood levels of lansoprazole or the other medications. Discuss all medications you are taking or have recently taken with your healthcare provider. If you or someone else has taken too much lansoprazole, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of lansoprazole, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Lansoprazole is used to treat heartburn and conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, erosive esophagitis (EE), and other conditions involving overproduction of stomach acid. It is also used to treat Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infections. Your healthcare provider may prescribe it for other conditions as well. Lansoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Lansoprazole is available as Prevacid, Prevacid 24HR, and generic lansoprazole in the following oral dosage forms: 15 mg delayed-release capsules, 30 mg delayed-release capsules, 15 mg delayed-release orally disintegrating tablets, and 30 mg delayed-release orally disintegrating tablets. Store lansoprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). It can be exposed to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) for short periods, such as during transportation. Lansoprazole capsules should be swallowed whole. If you have difficulty swallowing, you may open the capsule and sprinkle its contents on one tablespoon of applesauce, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. Swallow the mixture immediately without chewing. Do not mix the contents with other foods. If administered through a nasogastric (NG) tube, follow your healthcare provider’s instructions. Lansoprazole SoluTabs contain phenylalanine, a component of aspartame. Discuss the risks with your healthcare provider if you or your child is under one year of age, as younger children may be at greater risk for certain side effects. Before using lansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any prescription or OTC medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using. This will help them determine if lansoprazole is appropriate for you. Specifically, inform them if you have low blood potassium (hypokalemia), low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia), low blood calcium (hypocalcemia), low blood sodium (hyponatremia), liver problems, or phenylketonuria. Lansoprazole may cause common side effects such as diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, and constipation. Inform your healthcare provider if these side effects bother you. Serious side effects include kidney problems (e.g., acute tubulointerstitial nephritis), antibiotic-associated diarrhea (e.g., Clostridioides difficile infection), severe skin reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), lupus, vitamin B-12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia, and bone loss or fractures. If you experience symptoms of these conditions, stop using lansoprazole and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Do not take lansoprazole if you are allergic to any of its ingredients, including those in Prevacid, Prevacid SoluTabs, Prevacid 24HR, or other proton pump inhibitors. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients in the specific product you are using. Lansoprazole should not be used for immediate relief of heartburn, as it may take 1 to 4 days to fully work. Do not chew, cut, or crush lansoprazole. If you are also taking sucralfate, take lansoprazole at least 30 minutes before sucralfate. Antacids may be taken with lansoprazole if needed. Keep lansoprazole out of the reach of children. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Only take lansoprazole if it has been prescribed to you by a healthcare provider.
